ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Financial Transaction Reports Act (as amended, arts. 2-5 and 10-7); Act on Regulation and Punishment of Concealment of Proceeds of Crimes (as amended); Act on the Establishment of Financial Services Commission (as amended); Act on Prohibition of Financing for Offences of Public Intimidation (as amended); Korean Commercial Act (as amended, arts. 289-296 and 317); Foreign Investment Promotion Act and its Enforcement Decree; Personal Information Protection Act; supervisory guidance and examination standards issued by Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) and Financial Services Commission.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the Ultimate Beneficial Owner/Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Companies registry, corporate registrar, or competent state authority in the UBO's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: (i) notarize the certified copy of the certificate in the origin state, (ii) obtain an Apostille from the origin state's competent authority, and (iii) arrange a certified Korean translation; no consular step. Consular Legalization path for non-Apostille states: (i) notarize, (ii) authenticate through the origin state's foreign affairs ministry, (iii) legalize through the Embassy or Consulate of the Republic of Korea in the origin state, and (iv) prepare a certified Korean translation; the two paths are mutually exclusive and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of companies or equivalent commercial registry in the UBO's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: issue the certificate fresh, notarize if required, affix an Apostille from the competent authority of the issuing state, then translate into Korean by a certified translator; Consular Legalization path: issue fresh certificate, authenticate at the origin state's ministry of foreign affairs, obtain legalization at the Korean Embassy/Consulate, then provide a certified Korean translation; no sequential combination of Apostille and consular legalization is permitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution of the UBO/Parent Company approving Korean incorporation and granting Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the UBO's jurisdiction, authenticated by the UBO's board of directors and in accordance with its constitutional documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: notarize the directors' signatures and corporate capacity, obtain an Apostille from the competent origin-state authority, and attach a certified Korean translation. Consular Legalization path: notarize the resolution and signatures, have the origin state's foreign affairs ministry authenticate, then present to the Korean Embassy or Consulate for legalization, followed by certified Korean translation; the two channels are parallel and mutually exclusive.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association, Memorandum, or Constitutional Charter of the UBO/Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry of the UBO's jurisdiction or the notary public that holds the certified constitutional document
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: obtain a certified copy from the corporate registry or notary, attach an Apostille certificate from the origin-state competent authority, and provide a certified Korean translation. Consular Legalization path: obtain certified copy, authenticate through the origin state's foreign affairs ministry, legalize at the Korean Embassy/Consulate, and attach a certified Korean translation; apostille and consular legalization are alternative paths only and must not be combined.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the UBO/Parent Company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed relationship bank of the UBO/Parent Company, subject to FATF-compliant AML supervision and willing to authenticate the account relationship and standing of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille path: issue the bank reference letter on bank letterhead, countersign the manager's signature before a notary, obtain an Apostille from the origin-state competent authority, and attach a certified Korean translation. Consular Legalization path: issue the letter, notarize the authorized bank officer's signature, authenticate through the origin state's foreign affairs ministry, legalize at the Korean Embassy/Consulate, then provide a certified Korean translation; the two paths are exclusive alternatives and must not be layered.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening must be performed before incorporation and refreshed at least every 30 days for all natural-person UBOs, shareholders above 25% beneficial ownership, directors, executive officers, authorized signatories, trading counterparties, and beneficiaries of letter-of-credit payment rails. Screening must cover the OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List, the consolidated UN Security Council Sanctions List, the UK HM Treasury consolidated list, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, the Korean government autonomous financial sanctions designations maintained by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Financial Services Commission, KoFIU-designated individuals, and all persons named in public FATF statements. Enhanced due diligence is mandatory for any match, for high-risk jurisdictions, and for electronically valued shipments involving shredded non-ferrous scrap. PEP screening must identify foreign and domestic politically exposed persons, their family members, and close associates. Negative news and adverse media searches must be documented, and all screening records must be retained for at least five years after the relationship ends and reported to KoFIU if a confirmed match exists.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (IRO) of the Supreme Court of Korea, operating the official company name search and provisional company name registration through the district court registry system
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Korean corporate names must be registered in Hangul. A foreign-language name is permitted only as a transliterated English trade name used alongside the official Hangul name, and is not independently protected unless separately registered. A four-tier naming convention is applied: (1) a distinctive main trade-name phrase, (2) a business purpose or industry qualifier sufficient to distinguish the undertaking, (3) a geographical or descriptive element, and (4) the mandatory legal-form suffix 'Chusik Hoesa'. Under Article 23 of the Korean Commercial Act, an identical or confusingly similar name cannot be registered if it would mislead the public or be used for the same type of business as a previously registered company; the Supreme Court IRO database is the authoritative search source.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the district court registrar rejects the name application, the applicant may, within two weeks of receiving the written rejection, file an immediate appeal with the competent district court under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act. The appeal must state that the proposed name is not identical or deceptively similar to a previously registered name and that it does not misuse a prohibited or sensitive token. If the rejection is based on a sensitive token, the applicant should first obtain prior ministerial approval from the responsible authority and submit that approval with the appeal. If the appeal is dismissed, the applicant may file a new application using a more distinctive main phrase or adding an industry qualifier. The initial 180-day name reservation is not extendable by simple renewal; after expiration, a fresh reservation application must be filed, and therefore a rejected or fragile name should be abandoned before expiration so a subsequent reservation can preserve priority.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A pure virtual office or commercial mailbox-only address is not acceptable for a Korean Chusik Hoesa engaged in cross-border recycling and scrap copper wire wholesale. The National Tax Service requires a genuine business place for VAT, corporate tax, and e-tax invoice issuance, and banks will reject a mailbox-only address when opening a documentary LC or Swift TT settlement account. A serviced office may be accepted only if it includes a dedicated physical room, a lease agreement executed in the Korean company's name, office signage, a fixed-line telephone in the corporate name, board-meeting capability, and a demonstrable record-keeping presence. For the Middle-Risk Enhanced AML tier of non-ferrous scrap trading, the bank will normally require a physical inspection or video-recorded inspection of the registered office, employment records, and original lease documents.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection: (i) minimum one-year lease agreement in the company's name with actual exclusive or dedicated access; (ii) utility bills and common-area administrative charges in the company's name; (iii) at least one to two employees enrolled in the four Korean social insurance programs; (iv) original trade books, customs declarations, bill of lading files, weighing slips, and inspection certificates maintained on site; (v) VAT and e-tax invoice records aligned with bank transaction flows; (vi) scrap purchase and resale contracts, supplier qualification records, and LC receipts; (vii) physical warehousing or a written third-party warehouse agreement. Quantified risk: approximately 35-45% probability of a tax or registry inspection within the first 12 months for a fully compliant serviced or physical office in the scrap metal trading sector, rising to 60-75% for a mailbox-only virtual office. Inspections are usually announced in advance for routine tax audits, but the National Tax Service and Korea Customs Service may conduct unannounced spot checks of corporate books, VAT invoices, and trade documents where cash-intensive or high-value non-ferrous scrap transactions are suspected.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea, Book III, Chapter 3 (Stock Company), particularly Articles 289, 290, 292, 295, 299, 302, 310, 313, 317, 318, 331, 386 and 388; Commercial Registration Act and its Enforcement Decree; Foreign Investment Promotion Act (for non-resident investment); and the Waste Control/Transboundary Waste Movement Act for the licensed recycling-trading scope.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the Company's registered head office (for Seoul, the Seoul Central District Court Registration Office), with online filing through the Supreme Court Internet Registration Office (IRO) at www.iros.go.kr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Chusik Hoesa, together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation, minutes of the organizational meeting, share subscription and capital payment certificates, and consents of statutory officers, all submitted under the Commercial Registration Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital applies to a Chusik Hoesa. The subscribed shares must be paid in full before the incorporation registration is filed. Paid-in capital may be any amount agreed by the promoters, e.g., KRW 10,000,000, and must be evidenced by a bank balance certificate or a deposit receipt issued by a licensed Korean commercial bank. There is no general legal requirement for a blocked escrow account; however, a temporary lock-up/deposit account is used during the incorporation process, and where non-resident investment is made under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, the foreign capital must be remitted through a foreign-investment-capital account and reported. If a D-8 visa is sought, a practical threshold of at least KRW 100,000,000 of paid-in capital is typically expected by immigration practice.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service of the Republic of Korea (NTS), operating the Home Tax Service (HTS) electronic portal at hometax.go.kr; Korea Customs Service is the companion authority for export goods via the UNI-PASS single-window system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1. Foreign shareholders incorporate the Chusik Hoesa through the Korean commercial registration system and obtain the corporate registration number; file the foreign investment report under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act where applicable. 2. Within 20 days from commencement of business, file the Business Registration Application with the District Tax Office of the NTS having jurisdiction over the entity's Korean place of business. 3. Submit articles of incorporation, legal entity registration, address evidence, board resolution, foreign investment report or notice, and a notarized power of attorney if a Korean tax representative will handle tax affairs. 4. NTS issues the 10-digit Business Registration Number which serves as the single tax identification number for corporate income tax, VAT, e-Tax Invoices and customs purposes. 5. Complete Home Tax Service registration, obtain an accredited digital certificate, and enroll in the e-Tax Invoice transmission channel. When no fixed Korean place of business exists, appoint a Korean tax representative pursuant to the Framework Act on Taxes for all NTS filings and correspondence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None for entity classification; Korean Chusik Hoesa corporations do not have a US-style check-the-box election. Anti-hybrid mismatch rules under the International Tax Adjustment Act apply automatically without an election, while group tax consolidation election may exist for 100% Korean parent-subsidiary corporate groups.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value-Added Tax (VAT) under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No turnover threshold exempts a Korean legal person; VAT registration is compulsory from the date of business commencement regardless of revenue. Individual entrepreneurs with annual gross supplies up to KRW 80,000,000 fall under the simplified taxpayer regime, but a Chusik Hoesa carrying the present ISIC 4669 wholesale of recycled scrap metal is always a general VAT-registered taxpayer.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All B2B supplies by a registered business must be invoiced as an electronic tax invoice (e-Tax Invoice) transmitted to the NTS through Home Tax Service or an NTS-approved EDI/API service provider using an accredited digital certificate. The system validates and records the invoice at transmission; there is no pre-clearance stamping model, but the filing obligation is near real-time and export e-Tax Invoices must be associated with the Korea Customs Service export declaration. Anti-fraud enforcement relies on NTS analytics, UNI-PASS customs data matching, cash-receipt documentation for B2C sales, and penalty surcharges for failure to transmit or false transmission.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under the VAT Act, the cross-border supply of recycled shredded copper wire is zero-rated only when a Chusik Hoesa sells to a non-resident purchaser, title passes outside Korea, the goods are declared as exports through the Korea Customs Service, physically shipped from Korea to a foreign destination, and no domestic consumption occurs. The exporter must issue a zero-rated e-Tax Invoice, attach the export declaration reference, and settle the export proceeds from the foreign buyer in convertible foreign exchange through a Korean foreign exchange bank within the statutory settlement period. Qualifying offshore digital services are not within this ISIC 4669 physical-consignment scope and would require separate foreign-customer and foreign-currency tests.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service Export Declaration accepted via the UNI-PASS single-window system (customs export clearance certificate)
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill proving physical outbound shipment to the foreign destination
Commercial invoice with scrap copper wire specification, weight, and value reconciled to the customs declaration
Packing list for the shredded non-ferrous consignment
Zero-rated electronic tax invoice issued through the NTS Home Tax Service with export declaration reference

Foreign Exchange Settlement Certificate issued by a Korean foreign exchange bank evidencing receipt of foreign-currency export proceeds; the Korean banking equivalent of an inward remittance certificate
Documentary Letter of Credit or Swift TT credit advice matching the commercial invoice and customs valuation
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS and Korea Customs Service jointly verify export zero-rating through HTS and UNI-PASS data matching. A claim is invalidated if the goods never lawfully left Korea, ownership had not passed to a non-resident, the e-Tax Invoice lacks a valid export reference, or export proceeds were not repatriated from the foreign buyer by the statutory deadline. Invalidated zero-rating triggers assessment of 10% VAT on the supply value plus interest and additional tax under the Framework Act on Taxes, generally 20% if voluntarily revised and 40% if found through audit or non-disclosure; false e-Tax Invoice transmission also attracts VAT Act additional tax of 2% of supply value and revocation of prior refunds. Deliberate fabrication of export, customs, invoice, or foreign-exchange evidence is tax evasion under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and exposes the entity and its responsible executives to imprisonment or fines.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (central bank) together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance as the Foreign Exchange Control Authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act of South Korea
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea maintains a liberal but regulated foreign exchange system under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations. The Korean won symbol KRW is fully convertible on the current account for trade in goods and services, requiring only the submission of an underlying transaction report to a licensed foreign exchange bank. Capital account operations, including foreign direct investment, are free but subject to an advance declaration or post-review registration framework; inbound equity investment for a Chusik Hoesa must be registered with Korea's Ministry of Economy and Finance or delegated through the Bank of Korea to secure lawful asset protection and future profit outflow. There are no general surrender requirements for export proceeds, but exporters are obliged to receive foreign currency within 180 days from the date of export declaration and to repatriate the funds into a domestic foreign currency account or convert into KRW at the exchange rate determined through the Seoul Money Brokerage Services market. Dividend remittances to foreign shareholders are permitted after verifying the capital registration and completion of annual statutory audit, subject to a withholding tax under the relevant double tax treaty. Overall, the system presents moderate regulatory friction for illegal profit shifting but ensures clear clearance rails for genuine trade transactions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Export proceeds must be collected within 180 days from the date of export declaration. The full amount of the export invoice value must be either received into a domestic foreign currency deposit held at a Korean licensed foreign exchange bank or converted to KRW within the same bank. No mandatory conversion ratio applies to the recycled scrap copper export category, but every receipt must be traced with customs declarations, bills of lading, and bank receipts to satisfy a foreign exchange audit.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low feasibility. South Korean regulations require cross-border financial services and foreign currency operations to be executed through domestic licensed banks under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Offshore digital EMI platforms do not hold Korean banking licenses and cannot facilitate won-denominated settlement, capital verification, or trade finance instruments such as LC issuance. They may only be used as ancillary payment aggregators if they maintain a licensed local partnership, but are not viable as primary clearing rails.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of at least one statutory director and a beneficial owner is mandatory with a certified consulter or apostilled proxy; remote account opening via video call is not permitted for foreign-invested corporations in South Korea. Where the director is abroad, consular attestation at the Korean embassy or a permissible notarized power-of-attorney for a resident agent may be accepted, but the compliance committee will require a first-person interview at the bank before account activation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Economic or trade-based money laundering red flags: significant price deviations from London Metal Exchange copper wire averages in the export invoice and import customs declaration.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a signed purchase order and proforma invoice matching the bill of lading, an LME-sourced price evaluation sheet for the date of at least one week before shipment, a third-party weight certificate from a Korean customs bonded inspection agency, and a netback calculation proving the FOB price lies within a 5% tolerance of the index.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Legal ownership ambiguity: the Chusik Hoesa appears to have a bearer or trust-facilitated shareholding structure with no filed ultimate beneficial owners.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the certified Korean Company Registry extract, the stock ledger, a shareholder meeting resolution resolving all shares to named natural persons or regulated corporate shareholders, an AML/CFT self-certification for each UBO, and an undertaking that no anonymous shareholder or nominee arrangement exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex counterparty could trigger sanctions screening false positives due to recycled scrap connected to pass-through countries.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a complete chain of custody document from origin to export, including customs clearance statement of original export country, shipping manifests, an entity list with LEI-numbers of all supply chain participants, a sanctions-screening waiver or match remediation report from a commercial screening provider, and a low-risk country of origin certification issued by Korean customs for the scrap.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Frequent cancellation of letters of credit and cash deposits followed by immediate wire transfers to hidden accounts.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a treasury management file showing the bank the historical documentary credit lifecycle, a corporate resolution approving the conversion from LC to SWIFT MT103 only after delivery confirmation, an independent warehouse receipt for the goods, and a beneficiary bank confirmation letter proving the payee is an actual scrap processor, not an unlicensed metal trader.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Direct equity remittances must be executed by the parent entity's bank through SWIFT MT103 to the Korean bank's intermediary. The sender must use a purpose code equal to FDI-01 for investment into a domestic enterprise and include the Korean corporate registration number or foreign investment declaration reference. The receiving Korean bank will issue a capital import certificate, which is submitted to the Ministry of Economy and Finance or the Bank of Korea. The capital verification must be completed within 3 business days of receipt; any mismatch in the declared share issuance price will trigger a regulatory delay.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: All trade settlements with overseas counterparties should be cleared over SWIFT MT103/M202 for non-documentary payments, with documentary LC MT700/MT710 and documentary collections processed by the Korean issuing bank. For large consignments of copper scrap, use a confirmed irrevocable LC supported by a pre-shipment inspection certificate, or at minimum a sight documentary collection. All outbound disbursements over USD 10,000 must have a stated purpose code, and the underlying export contract must be made available for a random compliance audit.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore USD/KRW forward contracts executed with a Korean licensed bank for transaction hedging of forecasted exported scrap receipts, maximum tenor 12 months, requiring a real trade exposure and a rollover covenant.

Non-deliverable forwards referencing the Seoul USD/KRW fixing for non-resident counterparties via Singapore or Hong Kong clearing banks, available only for balance sheet protection of parent-injected capital, not allowed for speculative positions.

Cross-currency swaps between USD and KRW with actual principal exchange permissible if matched against the inward capital injection or a confirmed long-term copper supply contract, with the notional limited to 100% of underlying receipts.
FX options for hedging a known base metal purchase price, requiring bank confirmation of a real physical contract.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Ordinary General Meeting and approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Not applicable to a government filing; internal governance action with the assembled shareholders and statutory minutes retained at the registered office under the Korean Commercial Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year Chusik Hoesa, no later than March 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene the annual general meeting may expose directors to administrative fines under the Commercial Act, allow a shareholder or minority shareholder to seek a court-ordered meeting, and jeopardize the approval of audited financial statements; it is not an automatic strike-off event.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax and integrated Local Income Tax annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) with the competent local Korean tax authority through the integrated tax filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year company, by March 31, with an optional one-month extension to April 30 if the return is prepared and filed by a licensed tax accountant
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or underreporting triggers a 20% additional tax on the omitted tax amount, or 40% for fraudulent non-filing, plus daily overdue interest at the statutory default rate, tax seizure, compulsory collection and secondary director liability; a persistently dormant company with no business for five years may be judicially dissolved and its business tax registration administratively cancelled.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-Invested Company Annual Business Report where a non-resident holds 10% or more of the issued shares or exercises management control
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy (MOTIE) through Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (KOTRA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 for a fiscal year ending December 31; otherwise within three months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file is subject to an administrative fine of up to KRW 2 million; repeated non-filing may lead to revocation of foreign-investment registration and loss of tax incentives, but it is not an automatic strike-off trigger.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT Preliminary Return for January-March taxable period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April 25 of the same calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An unfiled or false VAT return triggers a value-added tax surcharge of up to 10% of the omitted tax, or 2% where payment is merely late, plus daily overdue interest; intentional evasion may result in criminal referral but not administrative strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT Final Return for January-June taxable period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: July 25 of the same calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An unfiled or deficient final VAT return triggers a surcharge of up to 10% of the omitted tax, daily overdue interest, compulsory collection of unpaid VAT and criminal liability for fraudulent returns; no administrative strike-off is imposed directly for VAT delinquency.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT Preliminary Return for July-September taxable period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: October 25 of the same calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An unfiled or false VAT preliminary return triggers the VAT surcharge of up to 10% of the omitted tax, daily overdue interest and enhanced tax collection actions; persistent evasion may trigger a criminal complaint and director disqualification proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT Final Return for July-December taxable period
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 25 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An unfiled or deficient final VAT return triggers a surcharge of up to 10% of the omitted tax, daily overdue interest, tax seizure and compulsory collection; intentionally false returns may lead to criminal referral and corporate deregistration through bankruptcy proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Interim Corporate Tax mid-year prepayment on semi-annual income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the first half of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year company, by August 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or pay the interim corporate tax liabilities triggers the same additional tax and daily overdue interest regime as the annual corporation tax return, with NTS collection procedures that may include garnishment of trade receivables and bank accounts.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: External Audit Report filing where the statutory audit threshold is triggered
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service (FSS) through the external audit disclosure system; the audited financial statements must also accompany the annual corporate tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: The registered certified public accountant must complete the independent audit and present the audit report to the shareholders at the annual general meeting; for a calendar-year company the report must be in substance filed before the March 31 book-closing deadlines
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to obtain or file the required external audit report violates the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies; the FSS may issue corrective orders, impose administrative fines, suspend the auditor, refer criminal charges, and for a listed issuer may initiate delisting; the directors cannot lawfully rely on unaudited financial statements.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Report under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act only if the Chusik Hoesa becomes a reporting issuer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service through the DART electronic disclosure system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end for a December-year-end reporting issuer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance by a reporting issuer triggers FSC enforcement action, administrative fines, criminal penalties and potential suspension of securities trading; a private Chusik Hoesa that is not a reporting issuer has no obligation under this item.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, Article 2, an independent certified public accountant audit is legally mandatory if, at fiscal year-end: (i) total assets equal or exceed KRW 12 billion, approximately USD 9 million; (ii) the company is a listed issuer on KRX or KONEX; (iii) the company is a financial institution, holding company, insurance company, or other public-interest company designated by the Financial Services Commission; or (iv) the company is otherwise designated for audit by the FSC under Presidential Decree based on revenue, total liabilities, employee count, or industry-specific public-interest criteria. Turnover and headcount do not operate as standalone statutory audit triggers in Korea but are used in the exemption evaluation for companies with total assets between KRW 5 billion and KRW 12 billion.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korean International Financial Reporting Standards (K-IFRS) as issued by the Korean Accounting Standards Board are mandatory for listed companies, financial institutions, and larger companies subject to external audit; non-listed smaller Chusik Hoesa companies not required to adopt K-IFRS may apply the Korean GAAP for Small and Medium Entities under the Commercial Act and the External Audit Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: South Korea does not currently maintain a general annual UBO filing for every private Chusik Hoesa. However, a statutory shareholders register must be maintained at the registered office and must be updated on every share transfer; no transfer is effective against the company until it is recorded in that register. In the foreign-investment context, a non-resident acquiring 10% or more of the issued shares must make a foreign investment report to MOTIE/KOTRA before closing, and any material change, including a transfer that moves foreign ownership above or below the 10% threshold, must be reported within 30 days. Banks and other reporting entities will also collect and periodically refresh beneficial ownership information under Korean AML and financial transaction reporting law as part of enhanced due diligence for a medium-risk cross-border recycled scrap metal trade.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders ledger) maintained in Korea
Register of Directors and auditors, including appointment and change historical records
Register of Charges or stock pledges where any security interest has been created, and corporate bond register if bonds have been issued
Minute Book of general shareholder meetings and board meetings
Commercial books, accounting vouchers, financial statements, and supporting statutory schedules for all fiscal years within the statutory retention period

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 - USD 2,500 per annum for an accredited corporate secretarial service in Seoul or Busan, covering registered office address, mail handling, AGM coordination, tax deadline calendaring, and UBO/foreign investment filing support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000 - USD 35,000 per annum for an independent certified public accountant audit of a cross-border scrap copper wire trading company whose asset size or business volume triggers the External Audit Act; USD 2,500 - USD 6,000 for financial statement preparation and review only where the statutory audit exemption applies

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% maximum marginal rate on taxable income exceeding KRW 30 billion under progressive brackets of 10%, 20%, 22% and 24%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Preferential tax holiday schemes under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act, including 50% or 100% income tax reduction for qualifying foreign direct investment in free trade zones; R&D tax credits up to 20-30% for qualifying research and development facilities; no patent box deduction, but the effective rate may be reduced by roughly 30-50% for eligible free economic zone activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Income Tax Return (statutory form for tax base and tax payable) filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic portal (www.hometax.go.kr); attach the financial statements, tax adjustment schedules, and Box 1-6 reconciliation modules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months after the fiscal year-end (March 31 for December fiscal year-end); a one-month extension is allowed for foreign-invested entities upon prior application; quarterly estimated tax prepayments are imposed on resident corporations.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total book income per Korean GAAP financial statements (business income before tax adjustments).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report the recycled scrap copper wire trading margin using Korean GAAP; include all intercompany invoice currency conversion adjustments and ensure that the arm's length allocation for the Korean selling activity is supported by a contemporaneous transfer pricing file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-deductible additions and nontaxable eliminations, such as entertainment expenses and donation excesses.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add back foreign director fees unless fully substantiated by service agreements, entry records, and operational evidence; deduct realized exchange gains only when legally recognized, and disclose all cross-border scrap consignment side contracts to prevent constructive dividend recharacterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable and deductible reserve adjustments, including bad debt reserves and employee retirement reserves.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany shared service charges from the offshore parent are deductible only when supported by a written billing schedule and an OECD compliant transfer pricing report; failure to establish economic substance yields a 5% gross-up penalty plus denial of the deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed taxable income before loss carryforward (tax base).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure that Korean-source business profit is limited to the activities actually performed by the local Chusik Hoesa and that no remote offshore entity creates a deemed permanent establishment; otherwise national tax authorities will reallocate income under Article 101 of the Korean Corporate Income Tax Act.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate income tax computed under progressive brackets, before credits and treaty exemptions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the 10%, 20%, 22%, and 24% brackets to the tax base; if foreign tax credits are sought for recycled copper transaction taxes, attach the original Tax Residency Certificate with sworn English translation for each affiliate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholding summary and foreign tax credit (FTC) claim schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List all outbound dividend, royalty, and interest payments and the corresponding withholding evidence; claims without a duly authenticated e-tax invoice or treaty-relief certificate will trigger denial of the FTC and a 10% negligence penalty on the credit amount.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 20% penalty on insufficiently declared tax (10% if only negligence) and daily surcharge at 10.95% per annum; non-filing beyond three months raises the penalty to 30%; fraudulent evasion or fabricated scrap invoices attract a 60% evasion penalty, criminal imprisonment up to 5 years, and personal travel-ban blacklisting for responsible directors.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% (20% national corporate income tax plus 2% local income tax surtax) on outbound dividends paid to a non-resident corporate shareholder, unless a lower bilateral tax treaty rate applies.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the Korean payer must file an application for withholding exemption with the local tax office before each payment, submitting the Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued in the foreign country within six months before payment, a beneficial ownership statement demonstrating that the foreign recipient is not a conduit, and the payer's certificate of corporate existence; the National Tax Service will issue a tie-breaker approval letter after verifying economic substance; if the reduced treaty rate is applied, the foreign shareholder must also file annual income declaration for the Korean-source income and preserve all contracts, invoice records, and board minutes for at least five years.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on outbound royalties for intellectual property and intercompany interest is 22% (20% national plus 2% local surtax); treaty rates commonly lower royalty and interest withholding to 10% or 15% when the recipient is the beneficial owner, but each payment requires the same TRC and beneficial-ownership substantiation as dividends; if DTA relief is procedurally breached, the full 22% must be remitted with penalties.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Korean Master File and Local File documentation is required where total annual sales exceed KRW 100 billion and related-party cross-border transactions exceed KRW 50 billion; a simplified Local File is required where international controlled transactions exceed KRW 5 billion; for a Chusik Hoesa in recycled copper wire trading, the national tax service expects contemporaneous documentation above KRW 1 billion due to the high-risk commodity classification.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korean tax enforcement applies the substance-over-form principle under Article 36 of the Framework Act on National Taxes and the OECD MLI for treaty benefits; the economic substance doctrine requires the Chusik Hoesa to perform real core income-generating activities in Korea, including local negotiations, logistics control, inventory risk assumption, and board decisions on scrap copper acquisitions; if the entity is deemed to lack substance, the National Tax Service may disregard its separate legal existence, deny treaty benefits, and reallocate profits to the offshore principal, subject to 30-35% penalty tax.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fraudulent under-declaration through artificial intercompany invoice booking
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating a shell offshore intermediary between the Korean Chusik Hoesa and the global buyer to artificially depress the Korean selling price for recycled copper wire, transferring the resulting profit to the offshore entity without any functional staff, assets, or risk absorption.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 61 and 76 of the Korean Corporate Income Tax Act and Articles 24 and 31 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, the taxpayer must pay the evaded corporate income tax, a penalty tax of 30-35% of the under-declared income, daily surcharges at 10.95% per annum, and a criminal fine equal to the amount under-declared.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Courts will pierce the corporate veil when the Chusik Hoesa is a purely formal entity; directors become jointly and severally liable for the tax, interest, penalties, and restitution of the offshore margin; the National Tax Service imposes a global travel ban and blacklisting on each director; participation in the false invoices leads to imprisonment of 1 to 5 years under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Failure to withhold and remit withholding tax on cross-border dividends, royalties, and interest
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Payment of dividend, royalty, or interest to the foreign parent without acquiring the Tax Residency Certificate, without filing the treaty-relief application, and without withholding the 22% statutory rate or applicable lower rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Article 127 of the Korean Corporate Income Tax Act, the Korean Chusik Hoesa is the withholding agent; failure to withhold triggers immediate collection of the withheld-remittance amount plus a 10% negligence penalty and daily arrears, and if intent is established the national tax authority adds a 35% fraud penalty and criminal prosecution.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who order or knowingly permit the unlawful remittance are jointly liable for the entire unpaid WHT and penalties; civil restitution of the remitted funds is ordered by Korean courts; a travel ban is applied while unpaid taxes remain; criminal imprisonment of up to 3 years is enforceable for misappropriation of tax, with each director's record struck in the tax violator registry.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell-company recharacterization and money laundering through circular recycled-scrap payment rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Chusik Hoesa as a treasury pass-through for documentary letters of credit and Swift TT payments that immediately flow to offshore parents without underlying delivery, insurance, storage, or processing activity in Korea, creating a classic cross-border circular trade and money-laundering pattern.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Financial Transactions Reports Act and the AML enforcement framework, the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit and tax authorities impose administrative fines up to KRW 300 million, require repatriation of the circular proceeds, and levy a 20% international tax coordination surcharge under the International Tax Coordination Law; the entity may be deregistered and permanently barred from import-export licenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The Commercial Act and judicial veil-piercing permit the court to disregard limited liability; directors are personally liable for all third-party claims, trade debts, and tax obligations; asset tracing from observed LC and Swift rails enables civil asset restitution; a travel ban is placed on every director during the criminal investigation; conviction under the AML Act carries imprisonment of 5 to 10 years, and each director's passport is seized and blacklisting remains after release.
